messages:
sara_customer: Hey team — we noticed a subtle change in the assistant replies after the model version bump yesterday evening. The customer (AcmeRetail) says responses are a bit more verbose and slightly more formal, which is breaking some UI copy flows. Example below (customer pasted):

sara_customer: BEFORE (v1.3.0):

  "Sure — I can add that item for you. Which color would you like?"

sara_customer: AFTER (v1.4.0):

  "Absolutely. I'd be happy to add that item to your cart. Could you confirm the color preference so I can proceed with the update?"

sara_customer: They call it a tone/verbosity regression — not a safety issue, but it affects downstream microcopy and increases token usage. They provided the API call too:

  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"retail-neo-1.4","prompt":"Add item to cart: item=1213","temperature":0.2,"max_tokens":60}'

sara_customer: Any ideas?

maria_support: Thanks @sara_customer — assigning. Can you confirm whether they used any system prompt or custom instructions? Also which rollout region (us-east-1)?

sara_customer: They said default workspace settings, no custom system messages. Region: us-east-1. Their account is on Hosted API, not Dedicated.

alex_k: Adding logs I pulled from the request id they provided. Looks like model id was retail-neo, version tag `1.4.0` (rolled last night at 22:10 UTC). Request payload matches what they posted. No error codes.

alex_k: Quick sanity check — I ran the same prompt against 1.3.0 and 1.4.0 from my dev account with the same params. I see the same pattern: 1.4.0 replies ~12–18 tokens longer and uses softer phrasing.

jon_eng_ml: Thanks for the repro, Alex. Possible vectors: decoding defaults changed (logit bias/penalty), prompting template updated during model packaging, or model finetune/LM head change causing more polite completions.

jon_eng_ml: Can someone paste the metadata from the 1.4.0 rollout config? I want to check default decoding params and any postprocessing hooks (e.g., normalize_whitespace, truncate_short_responses).

lisa_prod: Pasted from the deploy notes: "no changes to user-facing system prompts; default decoding: temperature 0.2, top_p 0.95, presence_penalty 0.0, frequency_penalty 0.0. Added a small normalization step to prefer full-sentence completions for short assistant replies."

maria_support: That normalization line sounds suspect. If it forces full-sentence completions, that could explain tone and token increase. Customer wants a quick workaround until we confirm root cause.

maria_support: Suggested immediate workaround: set `stop` tokens or reduce max_tokens and lower top_p/temperature to nudge brevity. Also can pin them back to 1.3.0 if absolutely necessary (requires approval).

jon_eng_ml: I'll run an A/B with normalization enabled vs disabled on a batch of sample prompts (incl. their prompts and a few others representative of UI microcopy). If normalization is the culprit it's a packaging postprocess we can toggle.

ops_bot: Auto-note: Incident ticket INC-2026-742 created for customer AcmeRetail. Priority: P2. Owner: jon_eng_ml.

alex_k: For repro, here's a minimal curl showing difference: 

  ```
  # against 1.3.0
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"model":"retail-neo-1.3","prompt":"Add item to cart: item=1213","temperature":0.2,"max_tokens":60}'

  # against 1.4.0
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"model":"retail-neo-1.4","prompt":"Add item to cart: item=1213","temperature":0.2,"max_tokens":60}'
  ```

alex_k: Sample outputs (redacted):

  # 1.3.0 -> "Sure — I can add that item for you. Which color would you like?"
  # 1.4.0 -> "Absolutely. I'd be happy to add that item to your cart. Could you confirm the color preference so I can proceed with the update?"

maria_support: Customer asked for a token delta estimate and whether it affects billing. Alex, can you quantify average token increase for their typical prompt set?

alex_k: Ran 50 prompts from their dataset. Mean token usage: 1.3.0 = 23.1, 1.4.0 = 34.7. That's ~50% increase for these short UI prompts. Cost impact non-trivial.

jon_eng_ml: That's consistent with a postprocessing policy that expands short answers. I can flip normalization off in a canary and push a hotfix to the packaging pipeline in <2 hours. But need sign-off from product for rollback or hotfix.

lisa_prod: Pinged @pm-team for approval. Given P2 and billing impact for an enterprise customer, recommend hotfix toggle first, then revert faulty change in packaging pipeline.

maria_support: I'll draft the customer response: acknowledge regression, provide workaround (pin to 1.3.0 or set manual `max_tokens` and `stop`), and tell them we expect a fix in ~2–4 hours. Sara, please confirm messaging is okay before I send.

sara_customer: Messaging looks good. Also asked for a short-term script they can run to auto-trim responses if they don't want to pin models. Suggest a regex to strip leading polite phrases? They'd prefer server-side fix though.

jon_eng_ml: Created quick toggle to disable normalization on canary; running tests now. If tests pass, we'll push to staged pool then full roll. I'll update thread with test outputs.

alex_k: FYI put their requests into a temporary policy override so their workspace will see 1.3.0 behavior while we fix global rollout. Doing this now.

ops_bot: Incident update: INC-2026-742 status -> investigating.

jon_eng_ml: Test results: canary disabled normalization -> replies match tone/length of 1.3.0 within ±2 tokens for 47/50 prompts. Two failure cases we need to inspect but not related to tone. Preparing PR to revert the normalization flag.

maria_support: Great. What's the ETA to have global fix and communication?

jon_eng_ml: ETA 3 hours to revert and run rollout. I'll attach regression check artifacts.

lisa_prod: I'll prepare a customer-facing note explaining root cause (packaging postprocess change), remediation (toggle rollback + optional pin), and offer credits if they want.

sara_customer: Thanks team. Please copy me on the customer note and confirm when override is removed.

maria_support: Will do. Closing loop once rollout is complete. :thumbsup:
